cues.text: Hi, I'm Sierra.
Here's how CPL Initiative funding works for your college.
The state set aside thirty-five million dollars in one-time funding.
About twenty-five million goes directly to one hundred eighteen institutions.
The rest funds statewide CPL projects, technology,
and two Chancellor's Office positions that support colleges.
Each institution has a maximum allocation for the two years,
from one hundred fifty thousand to four hundred thousand dollars.
The average is about two hundred fourteen thousand.
Each allocation splits into a credit share and a noncredit share.
Only noncredit outcomes count toward the noncredit share.
Two priorities carry the funding, in equal shares.
Access counts applied CPL units.
Completion counts transcribed CPL units, with the MAP counselor step checked.
The Chancellor's Office reports on career attainment together with the innovation projects.
The model sets each priority's statewide target from its funding and the FTES reimbursement rate:
about four thousand three hundred sixty-seven FTES for each.
Your college has its own target under each priority.
Thirty semester units of CPL make one FTES.
For the average allocation, the Access target is about thirty-four and a half FTES.
Reach half the target, and your college qualifies for half the share.
The full target qualifies for the full share, and that share is the ceiling.
The Chancellor's Office releases funding twice a year,
based on your college's CPL to date.
The full two-year amount is available from year one,
and what remains carries forward to year two.
You won't do this alone.
Every priority comes with recommended strategies,
a CPL Initiative help team supports every college, and detailed guidance will follow.
Find your college on the CPL funding page.
